calls.thesis: Expects a Q3 beat: AMD guided $13B plus or minus $300M at ~56% adjusted gross margin vs $13.12B consensus and $1.94 EPS, and he believes the CPU shortage is bigger than expected with Helios rack revenue starting to show. The Q4 guide (Street expects at least $16B) matters most; Meta's ~$1B partnership and Helios testing, plus share gains from Intel's supply failure via TSMC, support the long-term hold.
calls.price_at_call: No target stated; 30 Oct close ~$55 as cited (captions garble some figures)

calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY (he is a long-term shareholder): AMD is the biggest beneficiary of Intel's server-CPU shortage — its data-center-heavy revenue mix is the mirror image of Intel's client-heavy mix, its TSMC partnership beats Intel's struggling in-house manufacturing, and EPYC keeps winning share (Meta, Oracle). He ranks AMD his #1 pick of the four CPU names.
calls.price_at_call: No target or share price stated; cites AMD's reiterated guidance of 80%+ CPU revenue growth in H2 2026 and 70%+ for FY2027
calls.base_case: AMD keeps taking x86 server share while TSMC capacity (incl. doubling 2nm capacity in 2027) supports Venice/Verano ramps.
calls.bull_case: Intel's supply shortfall hands AMD outsized share gains and management raises guidance on the next print.
calls.bear_case: Capacity still below what AMD wants; a miss would contract the multiple, and a beat may not lift the stock much.

calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY / bullish: Meta announced a partnership with AMD including a $1bn equity investment in Meta as captioned and initial Helios rack-scale systems with the MI450 already installed and testing — he calls it a bullish indication, says Meta will use more AMD GPUs, CPUs and networking and co-design models, and later lists AMD among the big winners from Oracle broadening its AI stack with Helios. The $1bn figure is as captioned and should be treated with caution.
calls.price_at_call: No price stated; $1bn AMD equity investment in Meta as captioned

calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY (he is a shareholder): reported CPU price hikes by Intel, Qualcomm and AMD are extremely bullish — agentic demand far exceeds supply, so pricing restores balance and lifts margins.
calls.price_at_call: down ~2% on the day (no level stated)

calls.thesis: Lisa Su's Taipei comments (expanding CPU/GPU production, wafer capacity for several years of demand) add another 'brick' to his bullish thesis house; market wants constant confirmation and got it.
calls.base: Server CPU revenue expected to grow >70% in 2027; total data center revenue expected to more than double.
calls.bull: Server CPU TAM grew from $60B (Nov 2025) to $220B; MI450/Halos ramp with capacity build.
calls.bear: None stated in this video beyond general long-dated-guidance caution.

calls.thesis: $8.2B all-stock acquisition of World Labs (AI model/research lab) is a smart talent grab giving AMD deeper insight into evolving AI workloads and its tech roadmap. All-stock is the right call (<1% of market cap). Trusts Lisa Su's judgment; expects the deal to look smart in hindsight. Mild worry AMD is spreading itself thin (software stack, Helios ramp, now AI models).
